Great summary of many common fallacies, by the way.

From my understanding, in a scientific context, the burden of proof is placed on the party challenging the status quo

That is correct, the burden of proof always is on the person or persons making a claim, in any context where someone is attempting to make a sound argument. In the scientific context, the burden of proof is transactional. For example, a scientist makes a claim that they have identified an exotic particle, they then publish their findings and evidence. Now suppose another scientist learns of this discovery, but finds it contrary to one or more theories and claims that the first scientists discovery is invalid. The burden of proof then lies on them. The second scientist must present evidence of why the first claim is invalid, that may be due to finding errors in the study, or through their own experimentation (which would then be subject to the same sort of review).

The fallacy of shifting the burden of proof is indemnifying oneself of any need to provide initial evidence of a claim and making the opponent disprove it. When the opponent is unable to disprove the claim, the proponent declares victory, "you can't prove it wrong, so it must be true!" You often see this come up in religious/belief arguments, on both sides.

In the event that neither side is able to provide evidence to support their claim, then both arguments must be seen as weak or ultimately invalid.
